what: Lane S of the openai/math audit: every family with a Comparator challenge, its statements READ against the headline OpenAI wrote for it, the abstracts and OpenAI's scope note. A reading is not a certificate. Words, precedence and the second-reading rule are corpus/openai-math/preregistration.json (lanes.S, amendments 1 and 3); disagreements record the less severe word and show both.

rows.title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
rows.headline: Proves that every Dirichlet L-function, including $`\zeta(s)`$, is zero-free in $`\Re s\gt 7/8`$, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke L-function over $`\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})`$. A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane $`\Re s\gt 11/12`$.

clauses.clause: Proves that every Dirichlet L-function, including $`\zeta(s)`$, is zero-free in $`\Re s\gt 7/8`$
clauses.note: Every modulus q >= 1 ([NeZero q]) and every character (primitive or not, principal included); only the principal pole chi = 1, s = 1 is excluded, which the abstract also allows ("with the principal pole at s = 1 allowed"). q = 1 already contains zeta; QuasiRiemannHypothesis states it separately.

clauses.clause: resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
clauses.note: A fixed zero-free half-plane Re s > theta with theta = 7/8 < 1.

clauses.clause: The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke L-function over $`\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})`$
clauses.note: Characters encoded as multiplicative characters of O/m trivial on the image of the units; K = Q(zeta_3) = Q(sqrt(-3)) has class number one, so these are exactly the finite-order Hecke characters. The L-function is an in-file theta/Mellin definition (see flag).

clauses.clause: A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane $`\Re s\gt 11/12`$
clauses.note: As a statement, Re s > 11/12 is implied by the 7/8 statements; a "different proof" is not a statement. The 11/12 manuscript is not linked in the scope note, which is immaterial here.

rows.headline: Proves that Catalan's constant $`G=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2`$ is irrational.

rows.title: Ordinary two-point correlations and the corrected Elliott conjecture
rows.headline: Proves the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture, with a bound $`O(X/(\log X)^c)`$ for Liouville correlation sums along fixed nonproportional affine forms, where c > 0 is absolute. More generally, proves the binary corrected Elliott conjecture for complex multiplicative functions bounded by one when one factor is uniformly nonpretentious against each fixed Dirichlet character times $`n^{it}`$ for $`|t|\le X`$.

clauses.clause: Proves the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture, with a bound $`O(X/(\log X)^c)`$ for Liouville correlation sums along fixed nonproportional affine forms, where c > 0 is absolute.
clauses.note: liouville_log_saving: ∃ c > 0, ∀ nonproportional forms (a₁n+b₁, a₂n+b₂), ∃ C > 0, ∀ X ≥ 3, |Σ_{n≤⌊X⌋} λ(a₁n+b₁)λ(a₂n+b₂)| ≤ C·X/(log X)^c. Quantifier order matches the prose: c is chosen before the forms (absolute), C after them. The two-point Chowla case is a₁=a₂=1, b₁=0, b₂=h.

clauses.clause: More generally, proves the binary corrected Elliott conjecture for complex multiplicative functions bounded by one when one factor is uniformly nonpretentious against each fixed Dirichlet character times $`n^{it}`$ for $`|t|\le X`$.

rows.title: The Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture
rows.headline: Proves that the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, with the Ihara bracket, is freely generated by one element in each odd weight 3, 5, 7, …, resolving the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture.

clauses.note: ihara p q = D p q - D q p + [p,q] with D_p(x) = 0, D_p(y) = [y,p] (tangentLift).

rows.title: Function-field reconstruction from Milnor K-theory and Galois data
rows.headline: Reconstructs function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed constants from $`K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell`$, $`K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell`$, and their product. These data recover the perfect closure and constants when ℓ differs from the characteristic, and the original field and its named base in equal characteristic. Also proves Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction from abelian-by-central pro-ℓ Galois data away from the characteristic.

rows.title: Independent largest prime factors of consecutive integers
rows.headline: Resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture: the logarithmic sizes of the largest prime factors of n and $`n+1`$ are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density. In particular, the integers satisfying $`P^+(n)\lt P^+(n+1)`$ have density 1/2.

clauses.clause: Resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture: the logarithmic sizes of the largest prime factors of n and $`n+1`$ are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density.
clauses.note: joint_law: for every 0<a,b<1 the natural density of {n : P⁺(n) ≤ n^a and P⁺(n+1) ≤ n^b} tends to ρ(1/a)ρ(1/b) — the joint distribution function on (0,1)², i.e. independence with Dickman marginals. Both thresholds are powers of n (not n+1), an asymptotically immaterial choice.

clauses.clause: In particular, the integers satisfying $`P^+(n)\lt P^+(n+1)`$ have density 1/2.
clauses.note: increasing_order states it directly; decreasing_order adds the reverse ordering.

rows.title: Ostmann’s inverse Goldbach conjecture
rows.headline: Proves that no finite modification of the primes can be written as $`A+B`$ with $`A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z_{\ge0}`$ each containing at least two elements. This resolves Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture on additive indecomposability.

rows.title: The irrationality exponent of π is 2
rows.headline: Proves that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational $`p/q`$ satisfies $`|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-2-\varepsilon}`$. This also proves convergence of the Flint–Hills series $`\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)`$, with angles in radians.

clauses.clause: Proves that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational $`p/q`$ satisfies $`|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-2-\varepsilon}`$.

rows.title: Squarefree quartics and power-free polynomial values

rows.title: A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal’s function
rows.headline: Answers Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question: every interval of $`Ck^2`$ consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most k distinct prime divisors, for an absolute constant C. The bound is uniform over prime sets and interval positions and removes the classical logarithmic loss.

clauses.clause: every interval of $`Ck^2`$ consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most k distinct prime divisors, for an absolute constant C
clauses.note: Jacobsthal states exactly ∃ C>0 ∀ k≥1 ∃ m ≤ C·k² with every window {a,…,a+m−1} (a ∈ ℤ) containing an integer coprime to every n>0 with ≤ k distinct prime factors. JacobsthalImproved states the paper's stronger Ck²/(log log 3k)² bound (which implies the quadratic one since (log log 3k)² is bounded below by (log log 3)² > 0).

clauses.clause: The bound is uniform over prime sets and interval positions
clauses.note: C is quantified before k, n and a (∃ C ∀ k ∀ n ∀ a): uniform.

clauses.clause: removes the classical logarithmic loss
clauses.note: The quadratic bound (and its iterated-log improvement) has no log k factor.

rows.headline: Determines the optimal worst-case covering density as $`\Theta(n\log n)`$, for both lattice and unrestricted translative coverings. Every convex body in ℝn, n ≥ 2, admits a lattice covering of density at most $`Cn\log n`$; centrally symmetric examples in every sufficiently large dimension require at least $`cn\log n`$ even without the lattice restriction, for absolute $`c,C\gt 0`$.

rows.title: Subpolynomial dimension reduction in Lp
rows.headline: For every fixed $`1\lt p\lt \infty`$ and distortion D > 1, every n-point subset of real Lp embeds into $`\ell_p^d`$ with distortion at most D and dimension $`d=n^{o(1)}`$, answering Naor's sublinear-dimension question for p ≠ 2. In contrast, exact embeddings require worst-case dimension $`\Theta(n^2)`$ when p ≠ 2.

rows.title: The Gaussian propeller conjecture in every dimension
rows.headline: Proves that the sum of squared Gaussian first moments of any finite measurable partition is at most $`9/(8\pi)`$. In dimension at least two, three planar sectors of angle $`2\pi/3`$, extended orthogonally, attain the bound. Combined with the separate Unique Games theorem, this proves NP-hardness of improving the loss factor $`(8\pi/9)(1-1/k)`$ for identity-target kernel clustering with fixed k ≥ 3 on rational centered positive semidefinite inputs.

rows.title: The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström bound
rows.headline: Proves that any finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝd admits signs keeping every partial sum within $`C\sqrt d`$, independently of length. rows.title: The Unique Games Conjecture and optimal approximation thresholds
rows.headline: Proves Khot's Unique Games Conjecture. Independent direct reductions also establish NP-hardness, on unweighted graphs, of approximation beyond the Goemans–Williamson ratio for Max-Cut, below factor two for Vertex Cover, and within any fixed constant factor for Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set. These direct proofs use established PCP and Label Cover hardness results.

rows.title: Quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games
rows.headline: Gives deterministic algorithms using $`2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}`$ bit operations, for complete binary input length L, for ordinary mean-payoff games and two separate extensions. They compute exact values and optimal positional strategies in ordinary games, the nonnegative expectation-of-liminf value set in turn-based stochastic games, and the winning set for nonnegative liminf mean payoff conjoined with parity. Signed rewards, rational chance probabilities, and parity priorities are unrestricted and binary-encoded.

rows.title: Hardness of coloring three-colorable graphs
rows.headline: It is NP-hard to color a three-colorable graph using any fixed number c ≥ 3 of colors. More strongly, for every fixed $`0\lt \delta\lt 1/3`$, a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT produces simple unweighted graphs that are three-colorable in the satisfiable case and have no independent set of size $`\delta n`$ otherwise, where n is the number of vertices.

clauses.note: Implied, not stated: take δ = 1/(c+1) < 1/3; in the unsatisfiable case α(G) < n/(c+1) forces χ(G) > c, so a polynomial-time c-colourer for 3-colourable graphs would decide 3SAT through the reduction. 'NP-hard' itself (Cook–Levin for 3SAT) is outside Lean.

rows.title: A cubic permanent–determinant lower bound

rows.title: One-sample matroid prophet inequalities against an almighty adversary
rows.headline: For every finite matroid known in advance, gives a distribution-independent online rule using one independent sample per element and earning a universal constant fraction of the expected offline optimum. rows.title: Beyond the square-root exponent for depth-three circuits

This crosses the square-root-exponent threshold for explicit depth-three Boolean circuit lower bounds.

rows.title: Approximate counting and entropy of perfect matchings
rows.headline: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings in arbitrary finite simple graphs, with exact detection of zero counts. Also proves the perfect-matching entropy conjecture of Anari, Oveis Gharan, and Vinzant, bounding the maximum entropy of a matching law at every feasible edge-marginal vector in a loopless labelled multigraph, including boundary points.

For matroids presented by independence oracles, the results also cover common independent sets of prescribed, unrestricted, or maximum cardinality, even when the ranks differ.

rows.headline: At every fixed deletion probability in $`(0,1)`$, reconstructing an arbitrary length-n binary string requires $`n^{\Omega(\log\log n)}`$ independent traces, ruling out polynomial-sample reconstruction. rows.headline: Proves unconditional $`n^{\Omega(k)}`$ deterministic time lower bounds for joint and separate k-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence, for sufficiently large fixed k in the specified sequential adjacency-matrix models. rows.title: Talagrand’s expectation thresholds, discrete convexity, and graph decompositions

rows.title: Quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups
rows.headline: Proves that every finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group is virtually polycyclic, resolving the Eskin–Fisher–Whyte lattice-recognition conjecture. Equivalently, a group quasi-isometric to a lattice in a connected simply connected solvable Lie group is virtually a uniform lattice in some such Lie group, possibly a different one.

rows.title: The ionization and generalized ionization conjectures
rows.headline: For the full nonrelativistic Coulomb model with two electron spin states, proves that a molecule with M fixed nuclei of charges at least one and total charge Z strictly binds at most $`Z+CM`$ electrons. The energy cost of removing m electrons has Thomas–Fermi asymptotics as $`m\to\infty`$ and $`Z/m\to\infty`$; neutral-atom outer radii have the corresponding iterated-limit asymptotics, taking $`Z\to\infty`$ first.

rows.title: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
rows.headline: Constructs a uniformly discrete bounded-geometry space whose maximal coarse assembly map is not rationally injective. The example is a coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs of uniformly bounded degree, with an infinite-order kernel class. A companion gives the analogous failure for reduced coarse assembly, disproving the rational coarse Novikov conjecture.
